newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays rangebound in holiday trading.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays rangebound in holiday trading.

text.p: The ringgit remained rangebound in late Kuala Lumpur trading due to holiday in Singapore and Tokyo, dealers said on Thursday.
They said ringgit traded in a tight 10-point range for most of the day with most of the volume coming from Kuala Lumpur.
On an average day, a large part of trading in dollar/ringgit takes place in Singapore, the dealers said.
"The thin volume in dollar/majors in the Asian day did not help either," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said ringgit was expected to track dollar/majors in the near-term.
Singapore is closed for elections, while Tokyo is closed for week-long holidays.
"Nothing is happening because Singapore and Tokyo are closed. Dollar/ringgit will trade in a range for the rest of the day," said a dealer with another Malaysian bank.
He said it was possible that dollar would move down against majors in New York time, which could see ringgit gaining.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5262/67 a dollar.
